subject: Realtime sockets billing: per-minute vs per-request charge discrepancy
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@brightstream.ai>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 18:12:00 -0000
Subject: Unexpected realtime billing spike — need help

Hi Aditya / Ben,

We're seeing a sudden ~8x jump in our Redwood bill for Feb 19-20 tied to the realtime sockets endpoint. The token counts look normal, but the invoice shows an extra "per-minute" charge labeled "open-socket-minutes" which we've never seen before. This pushed our monthly consumption way over the expected range.

I've attached a small usage extract (usage_export_2026-02-20_2026-02-23.csv) and a screenshot of the billing line items (screenshot-realtime-metrics.png). Example session ids: rs-session-13a7, rs-session-13b2.

Can you confirm whether the realtime integration should be billed per request or per open-minute? If this is a metering switch on Redwood's side, we need a root-cause and a plan to correct the invoice.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Patel
Head of Platform
BrightStream AI
From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@brightstream.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 20:45:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Unexpected realtime billing spike — need help

Sam — thanks for the quick flag and for the attachments.

Quick answers up front: realtime sockets should be billed per logical API request token usage, not as a persistent per-minute socket charge. That said, there are two metering paths in our backend and a fallback can sometimes count session-presence as minutes for streaming integrations.

Looping in Ben (billing ops) to triage and propose remediation. To help us reproduce, can you: 1) confirm the SDK/library version you're using for sockets, 2) share a timestamped log snippet for rs-session-13a7, and 3) tell us whether you had any long-running debug sessions open during 02/19–02/20?

I'll keep this hot.

—Aditya Rao
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, Sam Patel <sam.patel@brightstream.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Feb 2026 09:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Unexpected realtime billing spike — need help

Thanks Sam — I pulled the usage extract and ran it against our metering logs. Two quick findings: 

- We have a legacy codepath (introduced during last year's streaming perf changes) that increments a "open-socket-minute" counter when an ephemeral session doesn't complete a graceful close within 60s. That counter is supposed to be suppressed for customers on the realtime sockets SKU, but there was a recent guard-condition regression that failed to apply the suppression for a small subset of sessions.

- The affected sessions (including rs-session-13a7 and rs-session-13b2) show repeated reconnects within short windows which amplified the minute counts.

Action items I'm proposing: 
1) Run a scoped recalculation for BrightStream for 02/19–02/20 to zero-out erroneously counted open-socket minutes.
2) Issue a pro-rated credit and an adjusted invoice.
3) Patch the guard condition and backfill tests to prevent recurrence.

I'm attaching our metering playbook excerpt that documents the two codepaths (redwood_metering_playbook.pdf). Sam — can you confirm the SDK version and paste the small log snippet Aditya requested?

-ben
Ben Carter
Billing Ops Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@brightstream.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai

Ben / Aditya — thanks for the fast investigation and the patch plan.

SDK version: bright-rtc-js v2.4.1 (we updated on 2026-01-15). We did have a short debugging window on 02/19 where an engineer kept a dev socket open for ~45 minutes; that might correlate. Attach: screenshot-realtime-metrics.png.

Log excerpt for rs-session-13a7 (timestamps UTC):
[2026-02-19T22:10:11Z] rs-session-13a7 CONNECT
[2026-02-19T22:12:52Z] rs-session-13a7 RECONNECT (code 1006)
[2026-02-19T22:15:04Z] rs-session-13a7 CONNECT
[2026-02-19T22:17:33Z] rs-session-13a7 DISCONNECT

Let me know what additional fields you need. We'd also like a short explanation of whether any tax/VAT treatment will change on a corrected invoice — we need that for our accounting.

—Sam
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@brightstream.ai>, ben_carter@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 22 Feb 2026 17:22:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Unexpected realtime billing spike — need help

Sam — appreciate the logs and context. Short plan and timeline: 

1) Ben will run a one-off recalculation for the 02/19–02/20 window to remove erroneously counted open-socket minutes.
2) We'll issue a credit for the removed minutes and post an adjusted invoice (credit memo) by EOD 2026-02-24. That adjusted invoice will contain the same tax/VAT line items as the original invoice; if your accounting needs a VAT-exempt correction we can route through our tax team but will need a quick confirmation from you.
3) We'll push the guard-condition patch to prod and include a short postmortem link in the HubSpot deal record.

Deliverables: recalculation run, credit memo PDF attached to the HubSpot deal, and a short summary email once complete. HubSpot MAC (mutual action plan) link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/DEAL-8942

If you confirm you want the VAT exception route, add a reply saying "VAT-exempt-correction requested" and we'll escalate to tax. Otherwise we'll proceed with the standard credit.

Thanks — we'll treat this as high priority.

Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
